06-10.solution: 21 L at \(5:2\) holds 15 L alcohol and 6 L water. For \(3:2\) the water must be 10 L, so 4 L is added.

06-11.solution: Alcohol is \(\frac{2}{5} = 0.4\) of A and \(\frac{4}{5} = 0.8\) of B; the target is \(\frac{3}{5} = 0.6\). By alligation A : B \(= (0.8 - 0.6) : (0.6 - 0.4) = 1 : 1\).

06-13.solution: Each replacement keeps \(\frac{32}{40} = \frac{4}{5}\) of the milk. After two, \(40 \times \left(\frac{4}{5}\right)^2 = 25.6\) litres.

06-16.solution: The 48 L hold 28 L alcohol. In the end alcohol is \(\frac{7}{16}\) of 48 L, i.e. 21 L, so \(\frac{7}{12}\) of the removed mixture is 7 L: \(x = 12\) litres.

06-17.solution: 40 L at \(9:1\) holds 36 L milk and 4 L water. For \(3:1\) the water must be 12 L, so 8 L is added.

06-4.solution: Take 2 kg at 24 rupees and 3 kg at 30 rupees: \(48 + 90 = 138\) rupees for 5 kg, i.e. \(\frac{138}{5} = 27.60\) rupees per kg.
